title: Verify audit evidence integrity / Configure audit-storage retention

blocks.text: CloudTrail integrity validation uses signed digest files and hashes to detect modification or deletion of delivered logs.

Use aws cloudtrail validate-logs with --trail-arn ARN, --start-time TIME, --end-time TIME and --region REGION for the supplied interval. For an organization trail, also supply the required --account-id. Inspect validation failures.
Digest validation provides tamper evidence; it does not prevent unauthorized access or deletion.

nodes.label: Validation command: trail, account, interval and Region
Signed digest and delivered log validation

blocks.alt_text: Make the validation command's trail, interval, Region and required account scope visible alongside the supplied validation results, with the seeded integrity failure identifiable.

blocks.text: A pass for one interval does not establish integrity for another. Preserve the seeded failure, with trail, account scope, interval and Region. Validation detects tampering; it is not access prevention.

public.prompt: What does CloudTrail digest validation establish about unauthorized access or deletion?

options.text: It provides tamper evidence; it does not itself prevent unauthorized access or deletion.
It prevents all unauthorized deletion once validation passes.
It replaces access restrictions because signed digests control who can read logs.

a.message: Correct. It provides tamper evidence; it does not itself prevent unauthorized access or deletion.

b.message: Tamper detection is not preventive protection.

c.message: Signed digest validation does not itself impose access restrictions.

correct.message: Correct. Your judgement follows the supplied evidence and the stated requirement.

incorrect.message: Compare the evidence with the requirement rather than inferring success from a partial signal. The validation targets the supplied trail, interval, Region and account when required. The learner identifies the seeded failure from the supplied validation results, preserves its evidence with the validation scope, and does not treat validation as prevention of unauthorized access or deletion.

blocks.text: S3 Object Lock retains object versions using governance or compliance mode and a retain-until date. Apply the supplied default duration and mode on the prepared bucket, then inspect individual audit-object versions.

During retention, compliance prevents deletion or shortening even by root. Governance permits bypass only with the necessary bypass authorization and request. Record each version’s mode and date rather than treating the modes as interchangeable.

steps.title: Review audit-object retention
steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which conclusions or actions are correct, defective or unsafe.

public.prompt: During an active retention period, how do governance and compliance retention differ?

options.text: Governance bypass requires the necessary authorization and bypass request; compliance prevents deletion or shortening even by root.
A governance bypass request alone suffices without bypass authorization.
Root can shorten compliance retention during the retention period.

a.message: Correct. Governance bypass requires the necessary authorization and bypass request; compliance prevents deletion or shortening even by root.

b.message: Governance bypass requires both the authorization and the request.

c.message: Compliance retention blocks deletion or shortening during the period even by root.

correct.message: Correct. Your judgement follows the supplied evidence and the stated requirement.

incorrect.message: Compare the evidence with the requirement rather than inferring success from a partial signal. The prepared bucket's default retention matches the supplied policy. Recorded version-specific modes and retain-until dates show whether the inspected audit-object versions remain protected for the supplied interval, with governance bypass distinguished from compliance protection. No unapproved retention settings are applied.
